If you can [compile from source](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.4/contributing/development/compiling/compiling_for_linuxbsd.html), there are two things which could be helpful to debug further:

- Build a known crashing version (e.g. 4.4-stable) with `scons debug_symbols=yes`, and paste the backtrace with debug information.
- [Bisect the regression](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/contributing/workflow/bisecting_regressions.html) between 4.4-beta3 (`git bisect good 06acfccf8`) and 4.4-beta4 (`git bisect bad 93d270693`).

The crash is indeed in the Nvidia driver so it's an Nvidia bug, but maybe if we can identify what causes it, we may be able to work it around.

That might be outside of my range. I will give it a try, but it might be faster if someone else did it!
 (I'm completely new to how to actually use Git, but I did give a quick glance at the bisection page)

I can confirm that I am seeing this from time to time using Godot 4.4.1.rc1. I am on Linux Mint but also using NVidia 550.120. I am not yet sure the cause. I will work on getting a debug symbols build if I can find some time.

I do not know for sure but I suspect my crashes may have been a red herring and that it was due to a logic error on my part. As of right now after applying some additional fixes it seems that my crashes have disappeared.

Update: Newest experimental version 4.5-dev1 does not crash! I was successfully able to create a new project and edit it! Now the question is, what exactly changed for this to happen?

Edit: Additionally I discovered a temporary workaround, by launching the editor via the terminal, and specifying a path to the project I wanna edit, circumventing the need to enter the Project Manager / project list!
 Quitting to the project list still crashes when it tries to open.

@FeralBytes That stacktrace is useful, but your issue seems unrelated to the one reported here indeed. Your crash happens in GDScript when resolving class inheritance, apparently triggered by loading a binary scene or resource.

I would suggest opening a new bug report with this stacktrace, but we'd likely need a minimal reproduction project too, or you to investigate which part of your GDScript code causes this to happen (e.g. by copying your project and removing parts little by little until it stops crashing, thus identifying which part makes it crash).

The backtrace is the part with `[1]`, `[2]`, etc. It has more details on frame 6, pointing at a location in the code. But does it really end there? There should be more frames/code locations listed afterwards that let us see what was the code path taken leading to the crash.

That being said it's a bit suspicious to go from `core/templates/rid.h:61` to a crash in the libnvidia-glcore.so driver, so I'm a bit suspicious of it.

Could you run Godot through `gdb`? It might do a better job at getting a clear backtrace than Godot's custom crash handler does. You do it with `gdb path/to/godot`, and then in the gdb prompt:
```
> run
// Then it should start and crash and give you a prompt back
> bt full
```
